taxonomy:
Below is a taxonomy for **grid-based logic / puzzle games**, organized by the *primary solving object* (placement of symbols, drawing loops, painting regions, routing paths, etc.). Each leaf includes one or more of your listed games.

---

## 1) Light / visibility / illumination puzzles
Rules center on what cells are “seen/illuminated” in straight lines.

- **Akari**  
  (place bulbs so all white squares are lit without hitting another bulb)
- **Kurodoko**  
  (numbered cells count white cells to nearest black/frame; black separation & connectivity)
- **Kurotto**  
  (numbers indicate connected black run lengths around circle cells)

---

## 2) Region filling & color/paint constraints (“paint cells” / “shade cells”)
Core action is shading cells subject to connectivity/forbidden shapes.

- **Choco Banana**  
  (black/white areas: monochrome rectangles, white adjacency restrictions, counts)
- **Hitori**  
  (duplicate numbers eliminated by turning cells black; black separation; white connectivity)
- **Heyawake**  
  (rooms; count painted cells; painted non-adjacency; line constraints on white)
- **Nurikabe**  
  (white areas labeled by size; black forms continuous wall; no 2×2 black)
- **Nurimeizu**  
  (walls/paint creates maze S→G; room painting; avoid loops/cutoffs; no 2×2)
- **Nurimisaki**  
  (circles are “promontories”; straight-line white counts; network connectivity; no 2×2 blocks)
- **Makaro**  
  (room-based number filling with arrow constraints)
- **Shakashaka**  
  (place black triangles in squares; uncovered area forms rectangle/square; adjacency counts)
- **Sto-stone**  
  (drop stones within rooms; continuous black cell constraints within regions; final packed bottom)
- **Tilepaint**  
  (tiles colored/uncolored consistently; diagonal-number ray counts)
- **Usowan**  
  (colored cells from rules; numbers constrain colored adjacency; each bold rectangle has exactly one wrong number)
- **Yajilin**  
  (loop avoids certain cells; numbered/black-cell directional restriction; black cannot touch)

---

## 3) Loop / cycle drawing puzzles
Core action is drawing a **single non-self-crossing loop** through grid cell centers/edges with region/turn constraints.

- **Dotchi-Loop**  
  (loop through all white-circle cells; straight-through vs right-turn behavior per bold area)
- **Masyu**  
  (loop turns at black/white circles with specific straight/turn requirements)
- **Nagareru**  
  (wind-direction loop constraint with arrows; loop cannot advance against wind)
- **Mid-loop**  
  (loop passes through all black circles with them as midpoints of straight segments)
- **Moon-or-Sun**  
  (loop cannot revisit rooms; per room uses either moons or suns; transitions between rooms)
- **Suraromu**  
  (loop must pass all gates once; starts/ends at open circle; gate numbers control order)
- **Slitherlink**  
  (single loop with edge counts around numbered cells)
- **Yajilin** (also fits here because it’s loop-based)  
  (single loop with restrictions around arrows/black/number cells)
- **Numberlink**  
  (path-network pairs with no crossings/branching; not a single loop per se, but “route-constraint”)
- **LITS**  
  (connected colored tetromino squares; resembles adjacency/structure, not a loop—kept in region/placement below)
- **Hebi / Yosenabe** (partially path/ordering; see “routing” sections below)

---

## 4) Routing / pathfinding puzzles (non-loop or directed single paths)
Core action is drawing paths from start to end or connecting points while avoiding collisions.

- **Hashiwokakero**  
  (bridges connect numbered islands; maximum two bridges between same pair; overall connectivity)
- **Hebi**  
  (place sequential snake parts 1→5; snakes can’t touch; arrow visibility/attack constraints)
- **Nagareru**  
  (loop-like, but wind-direction uses directed progression; included here conceptually as routing-by-direction)
- **Numberlink**  
  (connect equal numbers by non-branching non-crossing paths)
- **Pencils**  
  (pencil “rays” from tip with required length; cannot cross/branch)
- **Ripple Effect**  
  (room-based consecutive numbers with minimum separation when duplicated)
- **Satogaeri**  
  (move circles horizontally/vertically so each country has exactly one circle; pass-through counts; cannot cross tracks)
- **Yosenabe**  
  (move circles into gray areas; arrow shows movement; no crossing/bending; area sum of entering circles’ numbers)

---

## 5) Tiling / polyomino / shape placement puzzles
Core action is placing shapes (tetrominoes/tile-like blocks) in relation to regions.

- **Evolomino**  
  (arrows/blocks; fill blocks with growth by adding one square without rotation/flip)
- **Five Cells**  
  (partition into blocks of exactly 5 cells; line-count frame constraints)
- **Fillomino**  
  (each block filled with a number; block sizes by label; same-size blocks cannot touch orthogonally)
- **LITS**  
  (place tetrominoes inside bold areas; rotated/reflected similar shapes don’t touch except corners; colored connectivity; forbid 2×2+)
- **Chained Block**  
  (blocks of black cells; corner contacts create chains; no two blocks in a chain share same size/shape up to rotation/mirror)
- **Shikaku**  
  (partition grid into rectangles; each contains exactly one number = area size)
- **Double Choco**  
  (partition by solid lines; each block contains two congruent regions (white/gray) with counts equal to half of block)
- **Sashigane**  
  (tessellate with L-shaped blocks; open circle gives knee size; arrows point to knee; marks count 0–3)
- **Nurimeizu / Nurimisaki**  
  (also shape/region-based, but primarily are painting/maze constraints; already categorized in Region Filling)

---

## 6) Rectangle/room partitioning & block-structure puzzles
Core action is partitioning into “rooms/blocks” with local/global numeric constraints.

- **Heyawake** (rooms, counts, connectivity)
- **Nurimeizu** (rooms enclosed by bold walls)
- **Ripple Effect** (rooms by bold lines)
- **Shikaku** (rectangles by numbers)
- **Kurodoko / Kurotto / Makaro / Sto-stone**  
  (also heavily room/block based via bold boundaries)

(These overlap with other categories; the difference is that the *partition* is the main object rather than coloring or looping.)

---

## 7) Sudoku / exact cover style “Latin constraints”
Core action: assign digits with row/column/block uniqueness.

- **Sudoku**

---

## 8) Equality/adjacency / uniqueness constraint puzzles (graph/grid “logic placement”)
Core action is placing symbols subject to uniqueness or adjacency counts.

- **J uo s a n** *(Juosan)*  
  (fill with — or | marks inside territories; territory counts; direction-length constraints)
- **Choco Banana** (also paint + rectangle constraints; already placed earlier)
- **Usowan** (numbers constrain colored adjacency + exactly one wrong number per bold rectangle)

---

## 9) “Single-cell symbol constraints” / number placement without full region fill
Core action: decide placement of numbers in cells / apply local constraints.

- **Nansuke**  
  (fill blanks with given digits under row/column orientation constraints)
- **Makaro** (numbers placement into rooms, arrow-point rules)
- **Ripple Effect** (numbers per room, consecutive rule)

---

# Quick index (every listed game, placed once)
- Akari — Illumination  
- Chained Block — Tiling / blocks + chain constraint  
- Choco Banana — Region filling & shape constraints  
- Dotchi-Loop — Loop

- Evolomino — Tiling / polyomino growth paths  
- Five Cells — Tiling / exact block size  
- Fillomino — Region filling / numbered areas  
- Hashiwokakero — Routing (bridges graph)  
- Hebi — Routing / sequential snakes  
- Heyawake — Region filling + room partition constraints  
- Hitori — Region filling / uniqueness + connectivity  
- Juosan — Equality/adjacency marks within territories  
- Kurodoko — Illumination/visibility style counts + connectivity  
- Kurotto — Illumination/visibility style counts + run-length sums  
- LITS — Tiling / tetromino placement with connectivity & touch rules  
- Masyu — Loop  
- Nagareru — Routing/loop with directed wind restriction  
- Nansuke — Digit placement constraints  
- Norinori — Block placement in consecutive black squares  
- Nurimeizu — Region filling/maze walls  
- Nurimisaki — Region filling/promontories & network  
- Makaro — Room-based numbering + arrow max rule  
- Mid-loop — Loop  
- Moon-or-Sun — Loop  
- Numberlink — Routing paths connecting pairs  
- Nurikabe — Region filling / wall + area sizes  
- Nuritwin — Region filling with two blocks per region (twin blocks)  
- Pencils — Routing paths from pencil tips  
- Ripple Effect — Room consecutive numbers / separation constraints  
- Sashigane — Tiling with L-blocks  
- Satogaeri — Routing/movement of circles across tracks  
- Shakashaka — Region filling with triangle placement + rectangle/square leftover  
- Shikaku — Rectangle partition  
- Slitherlink — Loop  
- Sto-stone — Region filling with “drop”/packing and room constraints  
- Sudoku — Latin/Exact uniqueness  
- Suraromu — Loop  
- Tilepaint — Region coloring based on diagonal ray counts  
- Usowan — Region coloring with adjacency counts + one wrong number per bold rectangle  
- Yajilin — Loop with restricted cells/number/black touch rule  
- Yosenabe — Routing/movement into gray areas with sum constraints
